references.text: Terah took Abram from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan, which is the historical background for God's statement that He brought Abram out of Ur.
The Lord calls Abram to leave his country and his relatives, promising to make him a great nation – the beginning of the promise of the land.
After Lot separates from Abram, God renews His promise to give him and his descendants all the land they can see.
God confirms the covenant with Abraham and promises to give him and his descendants the entire land of Canaan as an eternal possession.
God uses a similar self-introduction formula: 'I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt' – parallel to the wording in the promise to Abram.
Nehemiah reminds us that God chose Abram, brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans, and made the covenant to give him the land – a direct parallel.
Abraham's faith in God's promises is highlighted: he obeyed the call and went out to a land he would receive as an inheritance, not knowing where he was going.
Stephen recounts that the God of glory appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia and brought him from there to the land God would show him.
The same theological formula links Abraham's departure from Ur with Israel's exodus from Egypt as the basis for the right to the land.
Nehemiah's prayer confirms and summarizes the historical event of Abraham's departure from Ur as described in Genesis.
